kind: A screen on the laptop's GPU, one seed: it chooses whether noisy thresholds earn two seeds on the server, and decides nothing about them by itself.
why: v15's walk from the Transformer to the stack priced the unit as its largest step (+0.0253 at full size, 9,000 updates, docs/STREAM_FORM.md), and a smooth plain unit alone recovered 0.016 of it in floats. The stack's threshold cells fire a staircase of whole counts and learn from the slope of a smooth threshold (GELU, one spike wide) that is a stand-in for a count that did not move; far below the threshold that slope even turns negative, so it tells a deeply silent cell to fall further when more of its spikes are wanted. A real neuron's membrane is noisy, so near its threshold it fires with a chance that rises smoothly with its charge, and its average rate is a smooth curve of its input. Under logistic membrane noise of half a threshold, a cell's average count is within 0.025 spikes of 0.5 * softplus(2 * charge / threshold) (tests/test_cell_noise.py), so the cell can learn from the true slope of its own average firing, and a cell a little below its threshold fires now and then and learns from spikes of its own. The noise falls with the learning rate, so that training ends on the whole counts that scoring fires; scoring is exact as always. Stochastic firing (cell_dither_with_data, randomness_at_best_rate) is a different noise: a uniform lift above the charge that never fires a cell below its first half threshold and keeps the plain slope. Does a cell that is smooth on average change the stack's slope over data at its best rate?

arms.noise: --cell-noise 0.5: every threshold cell adds logistic noise of half a whole threshold times the learning rate's share of its peak to its charge before it counts its spikes while training, and learns from the slope of 0.5 * softplus(2 * charge / threshold); 5,249,060 parameters, as the base

base: the delayed test bed trained on streams at peak rate 1.2e-3, seed 20003, on the laptop's GPU: rd-base-6k-s3 and rd-base-24k-s3, the base of randomness_at_best_rate's laptop seed and of gated_cells_with_data, trained and scored as this arm
training: the base's recipe (arm.sh's KIND stack, peak rate 1.2e-3, warmup 300, cosine over the run, pulse budget 113,000), 6,000 and 24,000 updates, seed 20003, the laptop's GPU (MPS), one run at a time after gated_cells_with_data's runs; code: the frozen copy of e5d3a1e that checkpoints/laptop-loop/run-queue.sh runs (v17l with the --cell-noise option added)
measure: experiments/eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams, lead 8,192, averaged weights, bits of every piece kept; the arm paired with the base of the same length; experiments/gap_by_piece.py splits each lead by what the context offers (near 240, far 8,192); the trainer's pulses a byte reported beside
reading: A screen with one seed. The arm earns two seeds on the server (s1 and s2, 6,000 and 24,000 updates, read by experiments/read_lead_study.py's shared reading against bed24-lr12 and rd-base-6k) if at 24,000 updates it leads the base by at least 0.005 and its lead at 24,000 updates is at least 0.005 larger than at 6,000. Otherwise it is reported only. Recorded either way: both leads, the leads on new contexts and on the fourth letter of a word on, and the pulses a byte at 24,000 updates.
seen_before_recording: CPU stress runs of 120 updates at peak rate 1.2e-3 reached after 30 updates (seed 20003, not a measure): noise 3.2897 in windows and 2.9880 on streams, base 3.3006 and 2.9963. The base's laptop run rd-base-24k-s3 stood at 1.7683 in windows at 10,500 updates; no arm of this screen or of gated_cells_with_data has trained. The full-size learning-rate pilot's pairs at 1.2e-3 and 6e-4 (full_size_rate_pilot.json) have been seen; they do not bear on this screen.
